How much does it cost to run an electric shower?

A typical electric shower uses about 9,000 watts (7,500–10,800W depending on the model). Used for 8 minutes per use, 14 uses a week, it costs about 32p per use and £230 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per use
32p
About £230 a year at 8 minutes per use, 14 uses a week.

Standing charge not included.

About these figures

Source for the typical figure: CSE 'What uses watt?' table. See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Heat the room you're in, with the door shut, rather than the whole house.
  • Use the thermostat and a timer rather than the highest setting.
  • Heating yourself (a blanket or heated throw) costs far less than heating the air.

Questions

How much does it cost to run an electric shower per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 9000W model costs about £2.37 an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run an electric shower per year?

About £230 a year, based on 8 minutes per use, 14 uses a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my electric shower's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
